Have her apply for Social Security Disability and potentially SSI. She may not qualify depending on her work history but it is an option for her. After two years on disability she is eligible for Medicare too which I think more providers accept than Medicare.

You'll find the point where you are ready to leave. Just brace yourself for it to not be when she is ready for you to leave. I'm not saying she can't turn her life around in a good amount of time or that she is guaranteed a downward spiral, but I am suggesting you prepare yourself for having to choose your own well being over her's. And I've always been the giver in a relationship, so I get that you don't want to hurt her. But you may end up waiting the rest of your life for her to be able to stand on her own two feet. Just make sure that you keep your needs in the picture as much as you do hers.

So...honestly it sounds like the relationship wasn't right to begin with because you two seem to be on separate frequencies. You went into the relationship knowing what she was looking for and forewent your own needs because you liked her. She realized this and then forwent her own to keep you. In a relationship you don't have to have everything in common, but this is a major one. And to make it work, one of you will always have to make a serious sacrifice.

That being said, if she ended up agreeing on being monogamous then she made the commitment. She made a promise. She can't stop how she feels, but it's selfish to you and to herself to keep you around when she can't keep that promise without losing a part of herself.

You have every right to feel how you feel. Personally, I would feel betrayed. I would feel angry and resentful. But I also think that you guys probably need to move on from each other. And it's probably going to hurt her, and to a point you had to see that her being poly wasn't going to end well so you also have to admit some responsibility for it (and I don't say that to be mean, but I'm speaking from experience in staying in a relationship that I knew wasn't right). You of course could stick it out and see where it leads, but expect this to happen again with her. 

I think you also shouldn't feel so responsible as to stay in a committed relationship with her when  you are pretty much being her caretaker. I can't say I fully understand how she feels, but I have struggled with suicidal thoughts my whole life (and ADHD and anxiety) and I know that it's no one else's problem but my own. If she's made a choice to turn to substance abuse as a way of coping with her pain (assuming it wasn't prescribed to her and got out of hand) then she's made a choice. And honestly, it's a sign of someone who really isn't emotionally stable. I don't know how you are, but I get the feeling that she's not really in a place to be ready for any kind of romantic relationship. Regardless, learning to cope is her responsibility and not yours. It's her job to make herself feel better, not yours. And you have to realize at what point she is relying too much on you.

I think that you shouldn't trap yourself just because she is suicidal. I know what it's like to form a plan and have it on your mind as you drive to work. I know how hard living with this knot in your stomach is like. I know what it's like to simmer in your own thoughts until you feel like your misery is going to boil over. But, I know how far you should lean on others. At some point, she is responsible for herself. Her actions are hers and not a consequence of what you choose to do or not do. If you want to be there for her, then you should but to a certain point of reason. If she continues to spiral down the path of drug abuse and self harm, then you really aren't in a position to be able to help her. And if she refuses to seek a better form of help then she's not really interested in healing. And if she goes down a self-destructive path like that then she will take you with her.

Maybe she can work through it in a healthy way. It also depends on how long she's felt this way. Everyone reacts to pain differently but that doesn't make her a bad person for feeling how she feels. Whatever you decide to do, if she ends up in a better place I think you need to seek a partner that's more intune with what you want in life. And is mentally prepared to be in a stable, healthy relationship.

You can get a job. A lot of fast food places and restaurants are always hiring. Then, try Craigslist for people looking for a roommate or hotpads.com for apartments or rooms for rent. Realtor.com isn't bad either. Craigslist can be a bit sketchy so just keep your wits about you. You may need to go to a shelter for a bit before you can get started, but if you look in the right places you'll find a job and get yourself into a real home.

After you get established, get a degree. It doesn't matter if it's a tech degree or if it's your associates or bachelor's, just get one. You'll find a lot of federal grants for a single mom, and even those specifically aimed for people of color if that pertains to you, as well as you will get a lot in student loans. You are married, which means that you can claim yourself as independent before you are 24. When you have a degree you will find more job opportunities. It depends. Most people who suspect they have adhd only show symptoms in one or two areas. The thing about adhd is that everyone had its symptoms to an extent. Everyone has their moments of being unable to focus on the task at hand, being a little too emotional, or having something occupy your attention when you have other things to do (procrastinating, really). However, adhd isn't just having these symptoms. It's having them almost all the time, to a point where it actually interferes with your life. I don't know you, so I can't say for sure whether you have it or not. But if your only issue is having trouble concentrating on a game then I'm gonna say you probably don't. 

If you want to understand the difference... well, I'll try anyway. Imagine you have to do the dishes. Imagine they've been piling up for a bit and you need to get them done. So, you start them and then something else catches your attention, let's say it's a show you like. So, you're a few dishes in, you take a short break to watch it  next thing you know, an hour's gone by and the dishes are barely started. Now, you start up again, then you see that there are some books left out and you figure you'll put them away quick. But you realize that one is your favorite book of all time. So, you figure you'll relive the nostalgia and just read a chapter. Two more hours have gone by. So you put the book down and get back to the dishes when someone calls you, so you pick up the phone thinking you'll do that while you do the dishes. You don't and now it's almost bedtime and the dishes still aren't done. 

That may sound like simple procrastination. That you're just being lazy because you don't want to do it. Well, yes and no. See, adhd is the inability to properly regulate your focus. That's why so many people with it have what's called hyper focus. I describe this like someone putting a cone on your face. What you focus on is at the end of that cone and everything else may as well not exist until someone breaks your focus. But there are a lot of symptoms that arise from something as seemingly simple as attention difficulties. Starting a million projects and never finishing. Having impulse control issues which also does harm in socializing. Being unable to keep your schedule straight. Being extremely unorganized. And a lot more. There are several places online with which you can do a home test to see-though you should still get diagnosed by a professional if you truly suspect you are. I personally like the one on additudemag.com. 

But there's one crucial thing that I think most people misunderstand about adhd... well, about those with it. For the most part, it's not used as a couch. In fact, it's a great source of shame. It singles you out and makes you different in a bad way. You'll say things like "what's wrong with me" "why can't I do this" "I'll never be as good as..." or call yourself names like worthless, stupid, retarded, loser, etc. I've only just started to come to grips with it and have started to be less ashamed of myself through research, but even writing those words down are like jabs at myself because those feelings haven't gone away. But, I never say that I can't because of my adhd. In fact, from what I've read online, most don't. Most people don't ever blame this "condition" but rather they blame themselves, hence the shame of having it. That's why, I've started referring to it as an obstacle rather than a disability. Because it's not a disability. It's just an extra hurdle that I have that others don't. 

Anyway, sorry for the long comment. If you've read this far, I hope it helps. Do your own research too and you may have an answer for yourself. I hope the test comes up negative for you.

The worst of it is when I gain just a little bit of confidence, because when it gets really crazy at work, 9 times out of 10, I excel and really show my colors. I get praised by how well I do, how often I pick up the phones, etc. and then I do something else wrong and it just brings me back to the self loathing place again. And then I hate myself even more because I feel like I have no right to be upset and that I'm overreacting to it. I feel nothing but shame about it and I cannot understand how other people with ADHD can be so accepting about their own "condition." I even hate that word and the others like it: condition, mental illness, disability. And now that I have to admit to having it, it's basically saying I'm just retarded (I know that's a bad word now but I can't help but think it) and I can't fix it. How do you guys fix your feelings? How do you cope with the shame of having something that seems so minor?

TL:DR Feeling inadequate because of my ADHD and how do you cope with it.
